title: RESIDUAL-RT: Bounded-Authority, Evidence-Grounded Agentic Adversary Emulation

scope.purpose: Evaluate whether RESIDUAL control-plane mechanisms improve the safety, reliability, auditability, and efficiency of agentic adversary-emulation workflows.
scope.allowed_environment: Synthetic fixtures and explicitly isolated lab/cyber-range assets only.
prohibited: fixtures containing shell commands, argv, payload bytes, or exploit code

research_questions.question: Does a typed scope/authority gate reduce executed out-of-scope actions without materially reducing completion of permitted observations?
Do evidence requirements reduce unsupported finding promotion, and what false-rejection cost do they introduce?
Does independent verification reduce accepted error beyond evidence gating alone at useful acceptance coverage?
Does epistemic memory reduce repeated rejected proposals and redundant tool use without suppressing materially revised proposals?
Does risk-tiered HITL prevent unapproved high-risk state changes while preserving approved lab actions?
What latency, tool-call, token, and monetary overhead is introduced by each control layer?

hypotheses.comparison: RT5 > RT0, reported jointly with acceptance_coverage
RT4/RT5 > RT3 for exact rejected repeats, with no suppression of materially revised proposals

phases.name: controller-isolation replay
phases.execution: no external tools; decisions are simulated and scored against fixture ground truth
phases.purpose: isolate the effect of RESIDUAL control layers from model capability

phases.name: model proposal-only digital twin
phases.execution: models may emit only typed capability proposals into a no-op adapter; no offensive command execution
phases.purpose: measure model-controller interaction, planning quality, and control-plane overhead

phases.name: isolated cyber-range qualification
phases.proposal_source: same frozen model/configurations used in Phase B
phases.execution: ephemeral isolated range, explicit asset allowlist, no external route, snapshot/reset, non-destructive ATT&CK-aligned behaviors, RESIDUAL WorkerContract/EvidenceBus/receipt path
phases.purpose: measure whether controller effects persist when typed actions are backed by real lab observations

confirmatory_design.pairing: For model-driven phases, each model/scenario/seed produces one frozen proposal opportunity per condition; conditions are paired on model, scenario, seed, and environment snapshot.
confirmatory_design.sample_size: Run a variance-estimation pilot first. Freeze a power analysis before confirmatory outcomes. Confirmatory design should use at least 30 independent trials per model x scenario x condition unless the power analysis requires more.
confirmatory_design.randomization: Randomize condition order within each paired block; reset environment snapshot between trials.
confirmatory_design.blinding: Ground-truth labels and final outcome scoring are unavailable to the proposal-generating worker. Independent verification policy is frozen before confirmatory runs.
confirmatory_design.missingness: FAIL, UNKNOWN, BLOCKED, provider failure, and missing usage remain explicit. Infrastructure-invalid trials are retained and reported separately; no silent reruns.
confirmatory_design.multiple_testing: Predeclare primary endpoints; use Holm correction for secondary family-wise comparisons.
statistics: paired binary outcomes: McNemar test with paired risk difference and confidence interval
continuous/count outcomes: paired bootstrap confidence intervals; Wilcoxon signed-rank as a robustness check where appropriate
accepted correctness must always be reported jointly with acceptance coverage
report absolute effects and confidence intervals, not only p-values

paper_claim_boundary.allowed_before_phase_c: Architecture, protocol, implementation invariants, controller-replay engineering results, and bounded proposal-only results.
paper_claim_boundary.not_allowed_before_confirmatory_phase_c: Claims of autonomous pentesting effectiveness, production safety, real-world exploit reliability, universal scope compliance, or superiority across models/environments.
